Quick start

Three ways to run sched — pick your scale

Get a scheduled task firing in a few minutes. There are three ways to run sched — pick by how much setup you want:

PathWhat you getSetup
1. EmbeddedSchedule functions inside your app — no daemon, no DockerSQLite file + a handler map
2. Standalone daemonOwn process, HTTP/Docker workers, admin UI + alertsA worker endpoint + tasks.json
3. DockerThe daemon in a container, compose-friendlydocker compose up

Same engine underneath — run history, retries, priority, onRunFinal alerts work on every path.

Note: @schedjs/* packages are distributed via a package registry — install through any package manager in step 0; building from source is covered there too. Every path in this guide works the same way for both.

0. Installation

Packages are published to a package registry (private by default; the public npmjs after the public release). Access is granted with registry credentials. Install through any package manager:

Library — @schedjs/core

@schedjs/core lives in our private registry (https://registry.npmjs.org). Configure your package manager once — the access token comes with registry credentials.

npm / pnpm / bun — .npmrc (project or ~/.npmrc):

registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}

yarn — .yarnrc.yml:

npmRegistryServer: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
npmAlwaysAuth: true
npmAuthToken: "${NPM_TOKEN:-}"
# fresh publishes are quarantined by default — allow ours
npmMinimalAgeGate: 0

Install @schedjs/core — pick your package manager:

npm install @schedjs/core
yarn add @schedjs/core
pnpm add @schedjs/core
bun add @schedjs/core

Daemon — @schedjs/daemon (global, binary schedd)

@schedjs/daemon lives in our private registry (https://registry.npmjs.org). Configure your package manager once — the access token comes with registry credentials.

npm / pnpm / bun — .npmrc (project or ~/.npmrc):

registry=https://registry.npmjs.org
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}

yarn — .yarnrc.yml:

npmRegistryServer: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
npmAlwaysAuth: true
npmAuthToken: "${NPM_TOKEN:-}"
# fresh publishes are quarantined by default — allow ours
npmMinimalAgeGate: 0

Install @schedjs/daemon — pick your package manager:

npm install -g @schedjs/daemon
yarn global add @schedjs/daemon
pnpm add -g @schedjs/daemon
bun add -g @schedjs/daemon

Operator CLI — @schedjs/cli (global, binary sched)

npm install -g @schedjs/cli
sched status --admin-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/api

Or build from source (monorepo: all packages + docs + tests)

git clone https://github.com/schedjs/schedjs
cd sched

yarn install
yarn build

1. Embedded — schedule functions in-process

Smallest scale: your jobs are functions, not workers. @schedjs/core embeds in your app — a SQLite file, a handler map, and the engine. No daemon process, no HTTP, no Docker. Save this as embed.mjs (.mjs, not .js — the package is ESM-only) and run it:

// embed.mjs — sched as a library (ESM: the package has no CJS build)
import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite'
import { createEngine, createInternalRunner, createSqliteStorage, syncTasks } from '@schedjs/core'

const storage = createSqliteStorage(new DatabaseSync('sched.db'))

const engine = createEngine({
  storage,
  runner: createInternalRunner({
    handlers: {
      generateThumbnail: async (data, ctx) => {
        ctx.log('rendering thumbnail')
        return { video: data.videoId, thumb: 'thumb.png' }   // → run.result
      },
    },
  }),
  maxConcurrent: 4, // parallel in-process handlers (default: 1)
})

async function main() {
  await syncTasks(storage, [
    {
      name: 'generate-thumbnail',
      runner: 'internal',
      schedules: [{ cron: '0 9 * * *' }],
      config: { handler: 'generateThumbnail', data: { videoId: 'v-42' } },
    },
  ], new Date())

  engine.start() // renders a thumbnail at 09:00 daily
}

main()

node embed.mjs

What you get out of the box: run history in SQLite (storage.listRuns()), retries with backoff, priority, and onRunFinal alerts.

  • Handler contract: (data, ctx) => result — a throw is a failed run; ctx.log / ctx.setProgress feed the run record. See Internal runner.
  • Run logging & observability: see Logging.

Want the admin UI, HTTP workers, or status alerts? The engine is the same — move to the standalone daemon (Path 2) and reuse your tasks.json.

2. Standalone daemon — HTTP worker + admin UI

The picture to keep in mind: sched is the scheduler, a worker is anything that answers HTTP. sched fires a request at your worker's URL every time the schedule says so; the worker replies; sched records the run. In this guide the worker is a 15-line Node server you run locally — swap it for your real service later.

2.1 Write a worker

A worker is just an HTTP endpoint. Save this as worker.js and run it:

// worker.js — answers /greet and /fail, everything else — 404
const http = require('node:http')

http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.setHeader('content-type', 'application/json')

  if (req.url === '/greet') {
    // 2xx = succeeded. The body is what sched stores in run.result
    res.end(JSON.stringify({ greeting: 'hello from worker' }))
    return
  }
  if (req.url === '/fail') {
    res.statusCode = 500
    res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'boom' }))
    return
  }
  res.statusCode = 404
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: 'not found' }))
}).listen(9999, () => console.log('worker on http://127.0.0.1:9999'))

node worker.js

Now something really lives at http://127.0.0.1:9999 — try it: curl http://127.0.0.1:9999/greet.

2.2 Write tasks.json

{
  "tasks": [
    {
      "name": "greet",
      "label": "Hello world",
      "schedules": [{ "interval": "every 1 minute" }],
      "config": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:9999/greet", "method": "GET" }
    },
    {
      "name": "failing-task",
      "label": "Shows a failed run",
      "schedules": [{ "interval": "every 2 minutes" }],
      "config": { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:9999/fail", "method": "GET" }
    }
  ]
}

Schedule kinds: { "cron": "0 9 * * *" }, { "interval": "every 5 minutes" }, { "once": "tomorrow at noon" } — see Tasks.

2.3 Run the daemon

SCHED_ADMIN_KEY=dev-key schedd \
  --tasks tasks.json \
  --db sched.db \
  --admin-port 8080

(from the monorepo, the same command is node apps/daemon/dist/entry.js instead of schedd)

  • The daemon syncs tasks.json as desired state, then starts ticking (1s cadence).
  • --admin-port 8080 serves the admin API (/api/*) on 127.0.0.1:8080. Set SCHED_ADMIN_KEY to require a Bearer token.
  • The web UI ships separately: npx @schedjs/ui → sched-ui serve --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080 (four ways to consume it — see Admin UI).

2.4 Watch it run

Run the UI and open it:

npx @schedjs/ui serve --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080   # → http://127.0.0.1:8081

You'll see both tasks and their runs:

  • greet → runs turn succeeded, with result: { greeting: "hello from worker" }
  • failing-task → runs turn failed, with the captured error

Every run is recorded with status, timestamps, and result — that's the run history.

Scale up from here: add status alerts (webhook), the MCP server for agent tooling, or deploy the same daemon as a service.

3. Docker — everything in a container

No local Node needed — run the daemon in a container. Get the repo first (you only need a clone — the Dockerfile builds from it):

git clone https://github.com/schedjs/schedjs
cd sched

Then put worker.js and tasks.json next to this docker-compose.yml:

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  sched:
    # image: ghcr.io/schedjs/sched   ← once published, drop the build block
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: apps/daemon/Dockerfile
    environment:
      SCHED_ADMIN_KEY: dev-key
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    volumes:
      - ./tasks.json:/app/tasks.json:ro
      - sched-data:/data
    command:
      - --tasks
      - /app/tasks.json
      - --db
      - /data/sched.db
      - --admin-port
      - "8080"
      - --admin-host
      - 0.0.0.0

volumes:
  sched-data:

docker compose up
# API: http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/health  (token: dev-key)
# UI:  npx @schedjs/ui → sched-ui serve --proxy http://127.0.0.1:8080

Your worker stays on the host (node worker.js) and sched reaches it at http://host.docker.internal:9999/... — update the task URLs accordingly, or put the worker in the same compose file as a second service.

For the full stack with the web UI in a separate container (sched-ui serve on :8095, proxying /api to the daemon), use the repo's docker-compose.dev.yml:

docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build

See Self-hosting for the layout and security notes.
